comparison: Perfect agreement on mechanical coupling coordination (C3, C19, C21-C30, C39-C40). Both evaluations find the experimental evidence compelling and well-supported with appropriate statistical methods and sample sizes. OpenEval notes specific technical details (50 Hz feedback, statistical tests), while peer reviewers emphasize the creative and remarkable nature of the validation.

Strong agreement on pause analysis and force-dependence (C4, C20, C32-C34, C43-C44). Both find the kinetic analysis well-supported. OpenEval raises minor concerns about subjective choices in pause identification method, while peer reviewers describe the work as exhibiting 'meticulous technical rigor' without raising methodological concerns.

Agreement on model validity (C6, C35-C38, C49, C64). Both evaluations support the modeling approach with no freely adjustable parameters. OpenEval notes dependency on pause identification validity and functional form assumptions. Peer review R3 also includes claims about simpler models (C60-C63, C65) that OpenEval addresses separately, but both agree on the necessity of persistent heterogeneity.

Both address model comparison claims (C60-C63). OpenEval evaluates the failure of the simpler non-pausing model as supporting evidence. Peer review R3 groups this with the broader modeling evaluation, affirming that pauses are essential to quantitative explanation.

Both address necessity of persistent heterogeneity (C65). OpenEval finds the ergodic model comparison supports this claim. Peer review R3 accepts the necessity of persistent heterogeneity without challenge as part of the broader modeling evaluation.

Divergent evaluations on in vivo extrapolation (C42, C52, C69). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting strong in vitro evidence but concerns about extrapolation to in vivo k-fibers and use of yeast kinetochores. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, affirming the conclusion about mechanical coupling coordination, though Peer R6 does raise concerns about yeast kinetochores being 'an odd fit' for studying mechanical coupling.

Agreement on experimental methods (C53-C55). Both find the 50 Hz update rate and force-clamp approach appropriate. OpenEval describes this as methodological validation. Peer reviewer requests clarification about bandwidth sufficiency but accepts the method, praising the experimental approach.

Divergent evaluations on methodological assumptions (C66-C68). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding bead tracking and kinetochore compliance assumptions well-justified. Peer review R6 rates as UNCERTAIN, raising concerns about using yeast kinetochores and recommending caveats, though acknowledging their utility for demonstrating mechanical coupling.

Both address contextual/background claims (C7-C10). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting these establish the biological problem with appropriate citations. Peer review R7 also supports these claims, requesting their inclusion to help contextualize the problem, treating them as established facts rather than novel results.

OpenEval rates mechanistic interpretations (C45-C48) as UNCERTAIN, noting they are plausible inferences and speculative mechanisms lacking direct structural evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific mechanistic claims.

OpenEval rates explanations for persistent heterogeneity (C50-C51) as UNCERTAIN, noting they are speculative hypotheses supported only by citations but not tested in this study. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific structural basis claims.

OpenEval rates speculative statements about division of labor mechanisms (C70, C72) as UNCERTAIN, noting they lack experimental support but appropriately acknowledge limitations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific mechanistic speculation claims.
